trip.title: Ajloun & Jerash Cultural Journey
trip.summary: A three-day exploration of Jordan's historic Ajloun and Jerash, featuring ancient mosques, Roman ruins, and local cuisine.

planning.strategy: Cluster-based itinerary with one day per region, focusing on must-visit sites and local cuisine.

poi_names: Al-Jubeiha to Balqa Agricultural Terraces Viewpoint

highlights: 13th-century Ayyubid stone minaret and vaulted prayer hall
Historic Islamic inscriptions preserved on inner walls
Active community worship center in historic downtown Ajloun
facts.notes: Non-Muslim visitors should avoid prayer times (Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Friday noon prayers).

highlights: 12 km comprehensive trek from highland forests to lush irrigated orchards
Opportunities to experience traditional rural Jordanian village life
Includes optional authentic local home-cooked lunch in Orjan village
facts.notes: Requires advance reservation with RSCN for guide arrangement and local meal preparation.

restaurants.name: Summaga Cafe & Restaurant
restaurants.address: Near Ajloun Reserve Entrance Road, Ajloun

facts.notes: Also sells packaged local organic oil, za'atar, and honey on-site.

poi.name: Ajloun Biscuit House
poi.address: Ajloun Reserve Crafts Village, Umm Al-Yandoub

highlights: Sampling traditional Jordanian olive oil and herb biscuits
Live Arabic calligraphy demonstrations by local female artisans
Handmade artisan culinary gifts made from organic local ingredients
facts.notes: Customized calligraphy requests can be done on-site in a few minutes.

restaurants.name: Ajloun Reserve Restaurant
restaurants.address: Ajloun Forest Reserve, Umm Al-Yandoub area, Ajloun

facts.notes: Reservations are highly recommended during weekend lunch hours due to ecolodge visitor traffic.

poi.name: Ajloun Olive Press Museum
poi.address: Heritage Street, near City Center, Ajloun

highlights: Authentic restored basalt and limestone animal-driven olive mill
Exhibits tracing olive oil production from the Bronze Age to modern times
Tasting area for extra virgin local olive oils and olive wood crafts
facts.notes: Especially active during the autumn harvest season (October - December).

restaurants.name: Al Kufa Traditional Cafe
restaurants.address: Old Quarter Alleyways, Near Great Mosque, Ajloun

facts.notes: The site lacks formal fences, ticket booths, or explanatory plaques. Visitors should be comfortable exploring raw, uncurated archaeological fields.
Includes an outdoor playground making it popular for families with young children.

poi.name: Al-Husun Traditional Pottery Studio
poi.address: Studio Lane, Old Commercial Quarter, Al-Husun

highlights: Live Traditional Hand-Thrown Clay Wheel Demonstrations
Authentic Recreations of Ancient Regional Terracotta Vessels
Working Local Wood-Fired Ceramic Kiln Units
facts.notes: Small groups can request short hands-on clay throwing trial sessions for a nominal fee if arranged a day in advance with the studio master.

highlights: Exposed Iron Age Fortified House Foundations
Panoramic Views of the Surrounding Highland Plains
facts.notes: The site sits directly on an open hill crest within the village boundaries. There are no visitor paths or fences, so take care around open trench edges.
Free Wi-Fi makes it a popular daytime workspace for university students.

highlights: Rotating Art Galleries Showcasing Regional Youth Talent
Intimate Cultural Event and Discussion Rooms
facts.notes: Admission to the regular art galleries is free, though special workshops or evening performance tickets may carry small independent charges.

poi.name: Irbid Central Souq
poi.address: Cinema Street / Wasfi Al-Tal Street intersection area, Downtown Irbid

highlights: Sensory Traditional Spice and Herb Stall Networks
Traditional Late 19th and Early 20th-Century Shop Façades
facts.notes: The area is exceptionally crowded with heavy pedestrian traffic and street vendors; vehicular parking is virtually impossible nearby, so visitors should rely on local taxis or walk from peripheral car parks.

poi.name: Yarmouk University Anthropology Museum
poi.address: Faculty of Archaeology Complex, Yarmouk University Campus

highlights: Extensive Historical Costume and Textile Trays
facts.notes: As the museum is inside the main university campus grounds, visitors may be required to present photographic identification at the university security gates for vehicle access.

hotels.name: Al-Jabal Castle Hotel - Ajloun
hotels.address: Castle Street, Halawa Crossing, Ajloun 26824, Jordan

facts.notes: Around 20 rooms. Approximately 2 km from Ajloun Castle and from the town centre. Barbecue facilities available to guests.

hotels.name: Ajloun Hotel
hotels.address: Al Rabadh Castle Street, Ajloun 26810, Jordan

facts.notes: 40 guest rooms. Continental breakfast is served daily for an extra charge and is not included in the room rate. Reviews rate location highly but room condition and cleanliness poorly.

Weekday overnight stay (Saturday-Wednesday): 200 JOD. Weekend overnight stay (Thursday-Friday): 250 JOD. Morning use (11:00-21:00): 170 JOD weekdays and 200 JOD weekends. Evening use (23:00-09:00): 120 JOD weekdays and 150 JOD weekends. Maximum capacity: 7 guests. Fire is permitted. Outside food and beverages are allowed. Optional Royal Decoration Package available for 30 JOD including cake, flowers, balloons, drinks, candles, romantic setup, music and bed decoration.

hotels.name: Ajloun Forest Reserve
hotels.address: Arjaan (Orjan) Village, Ajloun Forest Reserve, Ajloun 26810, Jordan

facts.notes: Operated by the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature under the Wild Jordan brand. Reservations are made through the Wild Jordan booking system. Hiking trails toward Orjan and Rasoun start from the accommodation area.

clusters.summary: Ajloun Governorate: 4 anchor + 6 discovery POIs; 8 restaurants; 4 hotels; 3 events.

highlights: Authentic locally produced olive oil and soap stalls
Traditional Jordanian handicrafts and embroidered garments
Street vendors selling fresh local produce and spices
facts.notes: Small shops generally accept cash only.
Features relaxing central fountain installations.
Excellent photography angle facing the ancient colonnades.

poi.name: Hippodrome of Jerash
poi.address: Adjacent to Hadrian's Arch, Jerash Archaeological Park, Jerash

facts.notes: Access is included in the general Jerash entrance ticket.
Located within walking distance of the ancient river crossing.
Renowned for traditional Jordanian feast platters.

poi.name: Suf Village Heritage Center
poi.address: Suf Main Village Square, Jerash Governorate

highlights: Local women's cooperative workshop producing heritage crafts
Tastings of local artisanal olive oil, thyme, and preserved foods
facts.notes: Directly connected by rural hiking trails toward Dibbeen Forest.
Overlooks dramatic natural canyon cliffs.

poi.name: Propylaea of Jerash
poi.address: Cardo Maximus, Jerash Archaeological Park, Jerash

highlights: Soaring Corinthian columns framing the processional entry
Triple stone door portals with carved friezes
Monumental staircase ascending toward Artemis Temple
facts.notes: Steps connect the Cardo street directly to the Artemis terrace.
Positioned conveniently close to the northern sections of the ruins.
Many independent shop owners close down business during Sunday morning church hours. The street is narrow and better navigated on foot.

highlights: Preserved ancient oil or wine pressing stones
facts.notes: The site is entirely undeveloped for mainstream tourism, unfenced, and integrated into modern village boundaries. Watch your step around loose rocks.

restaurants.name: Al Hadaf Family Restaurant
restaurants.address: Irbid Highway, near Northern Entrance Roundabout, Mafraq, Jordan

facts.notes: Includes dedicated private sections for family groups.
Cafe on the fourth and fifth floors with a panoramic view over the Jerash archaeological site. An ATM is available on the premises.
Formerly listed as The Country House Northern Gate. All rooms are non-smoking. Concierge service is offered.
Listed on the official Visit Jordan Jerash accommodation page. A grocery shopping service and an outdoor firepit are offered.

hotels.name: The Olive Branch Hotel
hotels.address: Guzn Al-Zaytoon Road, off Jerash-Ajloun Road, Jerash, Jordan

facts.notes: Family-run property with an on-site restaurant named Zaitoun. Room count is reported between 33 and 55 across different listings. Currency exchange, barbecue facilities and a games room with table tennis are available.

Jerash Festival for Culture and Arts

poi.name: Wild Jordan Center
poi.address: Othman Bin Affan St., Jabal Amman, Amman

highlights: Unobstructed panoramic terrace views of the Citadel and Downtown
Artisanal shop featuring local handicraft products from Jordan reserves
Organic dining options sourced from regional farming initiatives

highlights: Charming narrow hillside alleyways and staircases
Local orchards and peaceful neighborhood atmosphere
facts.notes: Residential historic area; respectful behavior toward local homeowners is appreciated.
Menu changes seasonally depending on local orchard harvest.

highlights: Located within the UNESCO-listed historic town zone

Large group seating capacity available; ideal stop after castle hill walks.

hotels.name: Al Hummar Restaurant and Hotel
hotels.address: Princess Tasneem Bint Ghazi Street, Al-Fuhays, Jordan

facts.subcategory: Restaurant with Guest Rooms and Events Venue
facts.notes: Primarily a restaurant and events venue with guest rooms attached, operating for around thirty years. Check-in is given as 14:00 by one channel and 13:00 by another. Fuheis sits near the Balqa and Amman governorate boundary and booking channels index the property inconsistently between the two, so the governorate assignment carries moderate rather than high confidence.

hotels.name: Jordan Heritage Madhafa
hotels.address: Al-Khader Street, Building No. 75/77, 19110 As-Salt, Balqa Governorate, Jordan

facts.notes: Six rooms in two categories, Classic and Panoramic. Check-in is accepted between 15:00 and 19:00, so late arrivals need prior arrangement. Free halal breakfast is included. Service animals are not accepted in addition to the general no-pets policy. Building age is given as over one hundred years in some listings and around two hundred in others.

hotels.name: Beit Aziz Boutique Hotel
hotels.address: Prince Al Hassan Bin Talal Street, As-Salt, Balqa Governorate, Jordan

facts.notes: Five rooms across two wings, of which four are listed as bookable on major channels. The house dates from 1905 and was restored after more than twenty years standing vacant. Sources conflict on whether breakfast is included in the rate, so it should be confirmed at booking. Craft-making and cooking experiences with local women are offered on site.

hotels.name: Saltus Hotel
hotels.address: Anis Muasher Street, 05315 As-Salt, Balqa Governorate, Jordan

facts.notes: Twenty rooms. The building has no lift. The whole property is smoke-free. Check-in time is given as 15:00 by one channel and after 14:00 by another. Wire transfer is accepted for corporate clients. Roughly forty kilometres from the Dead Sea.

meta.planning_lock:
PLANNING LOCK (hard — plan OVER clusters, then write JSON):
- Fill ALL 3 days (nights=2). No empty/partial days.
- Mandatory destinations (preferredRegions + mustVisit): Jerash, Ajloun. Plan ONLY in these areas — any other cluster is reference material, not a day.
- Destination→cluster map: Jerash→cluster 1 (Jerash Governorate · culture, history); Ajloun→cluster 0 (Ajloun Governorate · history, culture)
- Day→cluster route (one day per cluster, in this order): D1:C0/Ajloun → D2:C1/Jerash → D3:C2/Balqa Governorate · history, culture
- mustVisit entity lock: Jerash→lead with Hippodrome of Jerash (cluster 1)
- Each day draws its POIs, meals and hotel from ITS OWN cluster.
- No entity twice in the whole trip: a POI or restaurant used on one day cannot reappear on another, and lunch and dinner are different places. Two days in the same city are two different clusters — use each cluster's own entities.
- Each day: 3 sights + lunch + dinner (5 entries, 6 max). Two sights only when the cluster has no third worth visiting, and say so. No gap over 90 minutes, no site under 45 minutes, at least 4 hours of sightseeing per full day.
- activity_alternatives come from that cluster's UNUSED entities: never an entity scheduled elsewhere in the trip, and never two scheduled stops as each other's swap.
- One visit, one fee (POIs within 600 m are parts of one site): C0: Ajloun Great Mosque + Ajloun Olive Press Museum; C0: Orjan Soap House Trailhead + Ajloun Biscuit House; C0: Beit Al-Saraya Cultural Forum + Irbid Central Souq; C1: Jerash Heritage Souk + Propylaea of Jerash; C2: Fuheis Heritage Quarter (Al-Fuheis Old Town) + Fuheis Cultural Centre; C2: As-Salt Hammam Street + Abu Jaber Museum + The English College Building (Heritage Site)
- Lodging requested: rating=4 star, type=hotel. Per-night base (night N = where day N ends): N1(C0): Al-Jabal Castle Hotel - Ajloun [2-star] (4-star unavailable in this area — say it is 2-star); N2(C1): Celestia Boutique Inn [4-star]
- Money: 900 JOD covers 2 traveller(s) for 3 days (≈300 JOD/day for the whole party). Lodging = nightly rate x 2 night(s) x ~1 room(s), arithmetic shown in the notes. aiPriority=budget → take the cheaper of two comparable options and note the saving. SME=(none).
- Entry fees are the last thing to cut: never skip a named destination's main ticketed site to save money, and state what is left of the budget.
- Names/hours/fees: EntityCards only. If a card does not carry a fact (rating, booking requirement, closing day), do not state it.
- Prices: use the card value as-is, multiplied by the party size, and show the arithmetic in the tip ("10 JOD x 4"). If a card has no price, estimate from pricing_level and label it "~N JOD (estimated)".
- Events are reference only: never schedule them in the itinerary or budget.

geographic.clustering_rule: Keep each day geographically coherent. Avoid unnecessary cross-country hops.

budget.guidance: Comfort-oriented stays and dining when the catalog supports it.

climate.typical_pattern: High daytime heat, especially in the Jordan Valley and desert.
climate.outdoor_guidance: Schedule outdoor heritage and desert time in the morning; prefer indoor or shaded afternoons.

decision_rules: Never invent POIs, hotels, restaurants, SMEs, prices, hours, or coordinates.
Use only retrieved catalog IDs. If a needed item is missing, leave it unknown and warn.
Must-visit destinations are hard constraints unless impossible.
Honor places_to_avoid as a hard exclusion.
Target about 3 sights and 2 meals per day for a Balanced pace.
Recommend SMEs only when they are relevant to the traveler and the day's place.
Tourist relevance always outranks commercial promotion.
Avoid stacking outdoor sites in peak afternoon heat.
assumptions: Travel times between cities are estimated qualitatively, not as exact minutes, unless evidence exists.
Opening hours are used only when present on the catalog record.
